name: warmup_sweep
_comment: Does the 256 MiB ring reach steady state within the warmup we give it?
At the old 128 MiB ring the ltm_steady arm SATURATED -- ~100k evictions per
run -- so a plateau was guaranteed and 420 s was demonstrably enough.  A1
doubled the ring and evictions fell to ZERO, which removes that guarantee:
the cache may simply still be filling when the measurement window opens.
Repeats cannot answer this.  Every repeat is a fresh process that starts
with an empty cache and warms for the same duration, so two runs that are
both too short agree perfectly -- which is exactly what rep0/rep1 did
(802192 vs 776676 cached, hit 35.5% both).  Only a WARMUP axis answers it.
Read cached_records and hit rate across the three points.  Flat => the
ltm_steady numbers are steady state and quotable.  Climbing => 420 s is too
short for the bigger ring, and every A1 read number is a floor, not a
result, and steady.json needs its warmup raised before anything is quoted.
bf only: stock has no record cache to fill, and the question is solely
whether ours has stopped growing.  theta 0.9 only -- it is the slower
filling of the two and therefore the binding case.
